inicio.kicker: Selling with AI Program · course 3 of 5 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Foundations of Selling AI: sell trust, not building
inicio.lead: Building got easy. Trusting what was built did not. In eight lessons you swap the impostor feeling for your own proof, introduce yourself as someone who says what you know and what you don't, close without pushing, answer objections without discounting, and leave with a 30-day plan.
inicio.capa_alt: A consultant talks calmly with the owner of a small business, with the notebook open and the laptop closed.
inicio.aulas_sub: In the order for someone just starting: remove the block, define who you are, earn trust, prove it, close, answer, speak, and execute.

itens: People who know how to use AI but freeze when it's time to charge or start the conversation.
Consultants, freelancers, or technical professionals starting to sell to companies.
People who want to sell diagnosis, review, advisory, and teaching, not just "I'll build your agent."

blocos.t: What you walk away able to do
itens: Show your own proof instead of a pitch, without making up numbers.
Say in one sentence who you help, what you don't do, and when you call in a specialist.
Ask for the smallest yes, answer an objection by reducing scope, and leave every conversation with a date set.
Deliver a one-page report and follow a 30-day plan.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in Professional 2030
itens: Professional 2030 has four roles: Consultant, Auditor, Mentor, and Trainer. All four sell trust, not building.
This course is the foundation for all four: the identity of someone who diagnoses, reviews, advises on an ongoing basis, and teaches, and who says what they know and what they don't.
The common base it uses: ethics and limits (when to call in a specialist) and the one-page report.
